startups.name: Turnkey
startups.description: Developer infrastructure for key management, embedded wallets and programmable signing across crypto applications.

startups.name: Privy
startups.description: An embedded-wallet and onboarding platform that helps developers add crypto accounts and transactions to applications.

startups.name: Miden
startups.description: A blockchain project using local execution and proof-based verification to support scalable public and private transactions.

startups.name: RedotPay
startups.description: A stablecoin-focused payments business offering digital-asset spending, card and cross-border payout services.

startups.name: Rain
startups.description: Stablecoin payment infrastructure for businesses launching card, wallet and money-movement services.

startups.name: Mesh
startups.description: Infrastructure connecting wallets, exchanges and payment services so digital assets can be used for payments and settlement.

startups.name: Fission
startups.description: Blockchain-enabled infrastructure intended to improve liquidity for tokenized investment funds and private-market assets.

startups.name: KAST
startups.description: A financial-services platform built around stablecoin accounts, spending and cross-border money movement.

startups.name: Project Eleven
startups.description: Security infrastructure and migration tools addressing the implications of quantum computing for digital assets.

startups.name: Mesta
startups.description: A cross-border payment network combining fiat payment corridors with stablecoin settlement.

startups.name: Raise
startups.description: A gift-card and loyalty business developing blockchain-based payment and consumer-engagement products.

startups.name: Digital Asset
startups.description: The company behind Canton Network, building blockchain infrastructure for institutional financial applications.

startups.name: Walrus
startups.description: A decentralized storage protocol developed by Mysten Labs for storing data and supporting programmable storage applications.

startups.name: Boundary Labs
startups.description: A startup developing verifiable stablecoin infrastructure for financial institutions and approved participants.

startups.name: Octane
startups.description: An AI-assisted security startup focused on detecting vulnerabilities in blockchain software and smart contracts.

startups.name: Rena Labs
startups.description: Middleware for trusted execution environments intended to support private and verifiable AI applications.

startups.name: Multiliquid / Uniform Labs
startups.description: An institutional liquidity protocol developed by Uniform Labs for moving between tokenized investments and stablecoins.

startups.name: Credit Coop
startups.description: A lending protocol using business cash flows as collateral for blockchain-based credit products.

rounds.summary: Turnkey announced a Series B to expand its infrastructure for managing keys and signing transactions. The company said the capital would support hiring, open-source work and integrations for payments, DeFi and other onchain applications.
rounds.source_notes: The $30 million is this round’s amount. The announcement separately described lifetime funding of more than $50 million.

rounds.summary: Privy announced new backing led by Ribbit Capital for its embedded-wallet infrastructure. Its own announcement named returning investors and said the company had raised more than $40 million cumulatively, without specifying the latest round’s amount.
rounds.source_notes: Amount and stage are left undisclosed because the cited primary announcement does not give a standalone round amount or series label. The cumulative figure is not entered as this round’s funding.

rounds.summary: Polygon Labs announced Miden’s graduation from its incubation program alongside a seed financing. The announcement described a blockchain focused on public and private transactions, with founders moving the project into an independently funded business.
rounds.source_notes: The source is Polygon Labs, the incubating organisation. This is a funding announcement, not a mainnet launch date.

rounds.summary: RedotPay announced a Series A to develop its payment products and expand its geographic reach. The company identified Lightspeed as the lead and described plans to invest in compliance, licensing and the customer payment experience.
rounds.source_notes: The public announcement is dated March 14, 2025; it refers to a Lightspeed commitment made in December 2024.

rounds.summary: RedotPay announced a strategic investment with Coinbase Ventures joining existing backers. It said the capital would support payment corridors, partner relationships and licensing work. The round is tracked separately from the company’s earlier Series A and subsequent Series B.
rounds.source_notes: The release names participating investors but does not explicitly identify a lead. It claims unicorn status without an exact valuation, so no valuation amount is inferred.

rounds.summary: RedotPay announced a Series B for product development, acquisitions, licensing and international expansion. This round followed two other 2025 financings; the company’s stated annual funding total includes those earlier rounds rather than representing additional capital in this announcement.
rounds.source_notes: Use $107 million for this round, not the $194 million cumulative amount raised during 2025.

rounds.summary: Rain announced financing for stablecoin-linked card infrastructure. Its later industry-association profile identifies this as the March 2025 Series A. The company’s subsequent Series B and Series C are separate announcements in this tracker.
rounds.source_notes: The association’s member profile confirms the March Series A amount and sequence. The contemporaneous report establishes March 24 as the announcement date.

rounds.summary: Rain announced a Series B to develop enterprise stablecoin payment infrastructure. It described the capital as supporting product capabilities and expansion, following its Series A earlier in the same year.
rounds.source_notes: This is the $58 million round; the release’s $88.5 million figure is cumulative funding.

rounds.summary: Rain announced a Series C to expand the geographic reach and product capabilities of its stablecoin payment infrastructure. The release also disclosed a company valuation, which is recorded separately from the new funding amount.
rounds.source_notes: The cited Rain-issued release is a German-language distribution dated January 9. Its valuation basis is not explicitly labelled pre- or post-money here.

rounds.summary: Mesh announced a Series B to scale its crypto payment network and stablecoin settlement capabilities. The company said the funding would support infrastructure and commercial partnerships as it connected payment services with wallets and exchanges.
rounds.source_notes: The $82 million round is distinct from the announcement’s cumulative funding of more than $120 million.

rounds.summary: Mesh announced a Series C for scaling its crypto payment network and expanding internationally. Its own announcement reported a $1 billion valuation and total funding exceeding $200 million; the newly raised amount was $75 million.
rounds.source_notes: The company disclosed a valuation without explicitly identifying its pre- or post-money basis.

rounds.summary: Fission announced a Series A to increase liquidity capacity for tokenized funds and broaden its integrations. The company positioned the funding around reducing frictions that arise when digital investment products rely on slower redemption and settlement processes.
rounds.source_notes: Company-issued release distributed by PR Newswire. Descriptions of product activity are the company’s statements, not independently audited metrics.

rounds.summary: KAST announced a Series A co-led by QED Investors and Left Lane Capital. It said the financing would support product development, licensing and expansion across several regions as it developed financial services using stablecoin infrastructure.
rounds.source_notes: This listing uses the company’s public March announcement rather than a reported earlier negotiation date. No valuation is inferred from outside reporting.

rounds.summary: Project Eleven announced a Series A for post-quantum digital-asset infrastructure. It described plans for readiness assessments, migration tooling and a product release, following an earlier seed financing. The round is a funding event, not a claim that quantum migration is complete.
rounds.source_notes: The cited release is dated January 14; some regional distributions appeared January 15. The separate $6 million June 2025 seed is not counted in this round.

rounds.summary: Mesta announced a seed financing to develop its cross-border payment network. The company said it would use the money to broaden payment features, strengthen its teams and extend the network’s international reach.

Raise announced strategic financing led by Haun Ventures to develop blockchain-powered gift-card and loyalty services. The stated round amount is separate from the business’s cumulative financing, which the announcement described as exceeding $220 million.

Digital Asset announced strategic financing from financial-market participants and crypto investors to support Canton Network adoption. The company described the round as capital for expanding blockchain-based financial infrastructure and institutional participation.
rounds.source_notes: Digital Asset is a later-stage private business, included alongside earlier-stage startups. Financing stage does not imply a recent founding date.

rounds.summary: Walrus Foundation announced private token financing for its storage network. The capital was intended for protocol maintenance, ecosystem growth and application development. Because this was a token sale, it is separated from the tracker’s venture-funding total.
rounds.source_notes: Investor Raptor Group’s announcement was posted March 21; contemporaneous coverage dates the announcement to March 20. This is a private token sale, not an equity Series A.

rounds.summary: Boundary Labs announced a pre-seed financing for its institutional stablecoin infrastructure. The release described plans to accelerate USBD development and make verifiability a central part of its proposed product design.
rounds.source_notes: The announcement concerns development funding. A financing announcement alone does not establish present product availability.

rounds.summary: Octane announced seed financing as it emerged from stealth. It described using machine learning to identify and help resolve vulnerabilities in blockchain code, with the investment supporting its security product and company development.

Rena Labs announced pre-seed financing for its trusted-execution-environment middleware. The company said the funding would support technology development, recruitment and education around deploying privacy-oriented AI applications with blockchain infrastructure.

Uniform Labs announced the close of a seed financing for Multiliquid, its tokenized-asset liquidity protocol. The release reported total funding of $8 million across financings, without specifying the amount attributable to the newly announced seed round.
rounds.source_notes: The $8 million headline figure is cumulative funding. The current round amount is left Undisclosed and excluded from aggregate funding sums.

rounds.summary: Credit Coop announced a seed financing for its cash-flow-based credit infrastructure. It said the round would support engineering and business-development hiring as it expanded lending tools using programmable collateral and onchain settlement.
